title: The Evening Brief: Taylor retires a champion as records and reshuffles pile up
dek: Katie Taylor closed her career undefeated in her final act at Croke Park, while cricket, baseball, and basketball delivered record-setting performances alongside a wave of front-office and legal decisions across football and the WNBA.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The day's clearest throughline is closure and transition: a legend retired, a commissioner announced her exit, a suspended quarterback returned, and a contested legal ruling left college football's eligibility fight still open.
bottom_line: Saturday's clearest thread was closure paired with transition: Katie Taylor retired undefeated as a three-time undisputed champion at Croke Park, Cathy Engelbert announced her exit as WNBA commissioner, and Mark Sanchez moved toward resolving a pending criminal case with a guilty plea motion. Alongside those, injury reshuffled three rosters, Ben Simmons returning on a minimum deal, Harrison Smith back with the Vikings, and Shane McClanahan sidelined again, while the SEC's new federal lawsuit against LSU left college football's eligibility fight unresolved despite a favorable Louisiana ruling for LSU. The honest read is that today's record performances, from Mandhana's run tally to Clark's assist mark, are confirmed outright, while the legal and succession questions remain open by the reporting's own account. Watch the Alabama federal court on the SEC-LSU case, the WNBA's succession timeline running to December 31, and Oklahoma's step up in competition against Michigan on September 12.
body: Katie Taylor, 40, retired as a three-time undisputed champion on Saturday, September 5, defeating Flora Pili by unanimous decision (100-90, 100-90, 98-91) at Croke Park in Dublin in front of roughly 80,000 fans, the sixth-largest post-war boxing attendance recorded anywhere, per BBC Sport. Croke Park had not hosted boxing since Muhammad Ali fought Al Lewis there in 1972, and tickets sold out in 17 minutes when they went on sale in June, per The Guardian. Taylor closes her career with a 26-1 record.

Cricket delivered its own milestone a day earlier. Smriti Mandhana scored 124 runs off 64 balls against Hong Kong Women on Thursday, September 3, at the Women's T20 Asia Cup in Dubai, surpassing Mithali Raj's 10,868 runs to become women's international cricket's all-time leading run-scorer across all formats, with her tally now standing at 10,880, per BBC Sport. She continues the tournament Saturday against Pakistan.

Elsewhere, the day's stories fell into three groups: retirements and departures, roster moves shaped by injury, and legal fights over authority. WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert announced Friday, September 4, that she will step down at the end of 2026 after seven years that saw two collective bargaining agreements, three new franchises (Golden State Valkyries, Portland Fire, Toronto Tempo), and a salary cap that rose to $7 million, alongside persistent player criticism over her leadership and handling of abuse allegations. Mark Sanchez filed a motion to plead guilty in Marion Superior Court on Thursday in an Indianapolis stabbing case, days ahead of a September 8 trial date, with sentencing possibly falling on November 9 or November 16.

Injury-driven roster churn touched three sports. Ben Simmons signed a one-year, $3.5 million veteran minimum deal with the Sacramento Kings after 18 months away from the league, positioned as a mentor to rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr. Harrison Smith re-signed with the Minnesota Vikings on a one-year, $12.25 million deal (incentives to $16.25 million) for his 15th season, brought back after Jamal Adams, his designated replacement, tore his knee in the preseason opener. Shane McClanahan was placed on the 15-day injured list by the Tampa Bay Rays on September 5 with left forearm tightness, his second IL stint of the season, with Alex Cook recalled from Triple-A Durham.

College football's eligibility fight escalated. Judge William Jorden ruled Thursday that LSU may sign players who participated in NFL preseason, clearing Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris to join the roster and shielding LSU from NCAA or SEC sanctions. The SEC responded with a separate federal lawsuit in Alabama against LSU, coach Lane Kiffin, and athletic director Verge Ausberry, arguing the conference's own First Amendment rights are being compelled against its policy. Rutgers coach Greg Schiano said afterward, "We got outlicked, outplayed and outcoached. There is no other way to say it." Colorado also opened its season with a 14-13 win over Georgia Tech, freshman quarterback Julian Lewis throwing a late touchdown before the Buffaloes blocked a game-tying field goal as time expired. And No. 6 Oklahoma routed UTEP 51-0, John Mateer throwing three touchdown passes as the Sooners outgained the Miners 401 yards to 198.

Baseball and basketball added their own storylines. Luis Campusano's walk-off two-run homer in the 10th inning lifted the Padres past the Yankees 3-2, snapping a six-game skid in one-run games and moving San Diego half a game ahead of Arizona in the National League Wild Card race. The Cleveland Guardians organization recorded four walk-off wins in a single afternoon on September 4, three of them within minutes of each other in doubleheader nightcaps. Caitlin Clark recorded 14 points and 11 assists in her FIBA Women's World Cup debut as the United States defeated China 94-61, extending the American win streak to 31 games; her assist total marked the most by an American player in a Women's World Cup debut, per Sporting News.

At the US Open, results and off-court friction ran in parallel. Zheng Qinwen, ranked No. 121 after elbow surgery, rallied from a set down and erased a 5-1 deficit in the third set to beat No. 22 seed Madison Keys 1-6, 7-6 (3), 7-5. Anastasia Potapova upset No. 10 seed Amanda Anisimova 6-2, 7-5 in the same round. Aryna Sabalenka paused her second-round match on September 4 to complain to the chair umpire about a strong smell of cannabis on court, later beating Kamilla Rakhimova 6-3, 6-4. Naomi Osaka and Coco Gauff both addressed a separate crowd-conduct controversy involving roughly 100 credentialed content creators, with Osaka saying "If you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport," and Gauff calling for clearer etiquette guidance from venues and brands.

The reporting does not say why the SEC's Alabama lawsuit will resolve one way or another, nor does it say whether Rutgers' institutional financial strain (a reported $78 million deficit in 2025) will affect Schiano's job status; both are described as open questions the coming weeks will test.
Desk boards were unavailable this run, so all figures above are drawn directly from the day's published stories rather than a live scoreboard cross-check.

The coming days carry several concrete checkpoints. The SEC's federal lawsuit against LSU in Alabama remains pending and could reverse Thursday's Louisiana ruling. A sentencing hearing for Sanchez could occur November 9 or November 16 if a judge accepts his guilty plea motion. The WNBA must name a successor to Engelbert by December 31, 2026, or she extends her tenure into 2027. Mandhana and India Women play Pakistan on Saturday in Asia Cup group play. The US Open moves into its fourth round, where Potapova faces seeded Andreeva and Zheng faces another seeded opponent. McClanahan's forearm tightness and its response to rest will shape Tampa Bay's rotation depth into the stretch run, and Oklahoma's September 12 matchup with Michigan will test the Sooners against materially stronger competition than UTEP.
